title: A Preregistered, Artifact‑Backed Paired Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived, paired experiment (GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1) that compared LLM‑only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline on 200 stratified intent→configuration NetOps tasks executed in a Dockerized Mininet emulator with a deterministic validator. Under the preregistered, frozen protocol we produced one shared LLM candidate per task (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"). All confirmatory episodes were verifier‑accepted: baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200 (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729); exact paired McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Crucially, because the run used a shared single candidate per task (preregistered and executed as archived: execution/model_configuration.json, SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), no repair attempts occurred in the confirmatory trials; therefore the executed boundary condition documents reproducible behavior under that constraint rather than answering the broader question of repair efficacy when repairs are allowed to change candidates. We publish the complete preregistration (GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1, SHA‑256 d913b416...), execution manifest and raw artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl, SHA‑256 d76af611...), per‑episode LLM outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 9235bce7...), and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...). We explain why the confirmatory null arose, report the preregistered power mismatch, and describe precise follow‑up experimental choices (independent generation per arm, expanded validator coverage) that are required to test repair value.

sections.introduction: Automating natural‑language intent into device configurations is an operationally important NetOps capability but poses safety risks when generated configurations introduce reachability loss, policy violation, or service disruption. Architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair loops—generate→validate→repair (GVR)—are a common mitigation strategy. Prior NetOps LLM work and AIOps benchmarks motivate empirical comparisons, but these have often lacked preregistration, deterministic artifact publication, or paired within‑task designs that control sampling variance. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to quantify GVR benefit under a frozen design and to publish all artifacts so the exact run is reproducible.
sections.related_work: We position this study relative to (1) recent NetOps intent→configuration evaluations and benchmarks (e.g., NetConfEval; OpsEval; NetEval) which examine translation accuracy and overall model capability; (2) verifier‑assisted and RAG‑style pipelines that target reduced hallucination and guarded execution; and (3) software generate→validate→repair literature that informs repair-loop design and evaluation. Unlike prior work, we (a) preregistered design, (b) froze generation semantics and retry policies, (c) executed a deterministic paired analysis, and (d) archived all raw artifacts and hashes to permit byte‑for‑byte reproduction.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental plan. The study was preregistered as GVR‑ProtocolEval‑2026‑PR1; preregistration JSON and SHA‑256 are archived (SHA‑256 d913b4167cc6...). The confirmatory design was a stratified paired comparison on 200 tasks (10 clusters: 5 protocol families × 2 modalities). Primary estimand: paired difference in a binary operational‑failure indicator (1 if the deterministic validator reports reachability or policy failure; 0 otherwise). Inference: paired bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and exact McNemar test as preregistered. Key frozen decisions (published and enforced): generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate generated per task and evaluated under both conditions), maximum_model_calls = 400, and retry policy limited to infrastructure recoveries. The preregistered power plan targeted an absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points with 80% power; that calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate and a conservative within‑task correlation (ρ≈0.5).
sections.results: Execution and archival. We executed the frozen plan in a Dockerized Mininet emulator and used gpt‑5‑mini for generation (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611...). Confirmatory outcomes. Planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 arms). Completed episodes = 400; model calls used = 200 (one shared candidate per task as preregistered). Scoring summary (analysis artifacts): baseline verifier‑accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier‑accepted = 200/200. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary inference: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact paired McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative artifact examples. Three representative confirmatory episodes and their artifact hashes are included in the archive and referenced in the Evidence Bundle: task-000001 (shared response SHA‑256 f8de4d6e..., scoring JSON SHA‑256 9235bce7...), task-000002 (shared response SHA‑256 ae967f70..., scoring JSON SHA‑256 25e2c0c7...), task-000003 (shared response SHA‑256 f7f4db24..., scoring JSON SHA‑256 20e953b1...). Each scoring JSON includes the deterministic validator trace that records parsed commands, required checks, and the validator verdict.
sections.discussion: Why did the confirmatory paired difference equal zero? The executed boundary condition (shared_initial_candidate) was preregistered and enforced: a single LLM candidate per confirmatory task was generated and then scored under both the baseline and guarded arms (this conserved model calls). Consequently repair_applied = false for all confirmatory episodes and no repair‑driven divergence could occur; the run therefore records reproducible acceptance of the shared candidates rather than the effect of active repairs. The reviewer critique that this design prevented testing repair efficacy is correct and anticipated: the preregistration explicitly recorded generation_semantics and this was executed verbatim (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2... and execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611...). Potential explanations for baseline=100% (artifact‑grounded diagnostics): (1) validator permissiveness or insufficient challenge: validator checks exercised per scoring JSONs show only the preregistered finite rule set; representative validator traces are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 9235bce7..., execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json SHA‑256 25e2c0c7..., execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json SHA‑256 20e953b1...) and permit external inspection of which rules fired; (2) task template solvability and model capability: the synthetic task templates and LLM candidate contents (execution/responses/*.txt SHA‑256 listed in the execution manifest) show that generated candidates matched the validator's expected command sequences for these templates; (3) contamination/memorization risk: automated contamination checks (token‑overlap threshold ≥80%) flagged no confirmatory exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...), but nondiscoverable pretraining overlap cannot be fully excluded. Power and inference consequences. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate; observed baseline success = 100% violates that assumption and makes the preregistered MDE unattainable in this run. We therefore report the exact observed contingency and CIs and explicitly state that the planned MDE target was not testable given observed data. Operational implications and what the run does show. The run documents that under a strict shared‑candidate boundary and the chosen validator/emulator, the LLM produced verifier‑acceptable candidates for all sampled tasks. That outcome is operationally interesting in a narrow sense (one can conserve model calls by sharing a vetted candidate across conditions), but it does not validate the incremental value of active repair loops. Follow‑up experiments needed to evaluate repair value. To measure repair efficacy the archived artifacts enable two minimal, preregisterable changes: (A) independent_generation_per_arm = true (generate separate LLM outputs per arm so repairs may modify acceptance), and (B) expand validator rule coverage and emulator fidelity to capture timing, vendor‑syntax, and side‑effect checks. All artifacts required to implement and reproduce such follow‑ups are archived and hashed in the execution bundle (execution/*, analysis/*). Reproducibility and artifact availability. We publish: the full preregistration with SHA‑256 d913b4167cc6..., the execution manifest and raw outputs (execution/execution_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 d76af611...), per‑episode scoring JSONs and validator traces (example execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 9235bce7...), per‑episode response files (execution/responses/*.txt), provider call traces, and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...). These artifacts permit exact deterministic replays and principled follow‑ups.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an autonomous paired study comparing LLM‑only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline across 200 stratified NetOps tasks under a frozen boundary in which one shared LLM candidate per task was generated and scored under both arms. Observed confirmatory outcomes were identical acceptance in both arms (n11=200), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 with a 95% bootstrap CI of [0.00,0.00] and McNemar p = 1.0. This null is a direct consequence of the executed shared‑generation semantics (no repair attempts in confirmatory episodes) and does not settle whether active repair loops improve operational acceptance when they can modify candidates. We provide the full preregistration, execution manifest, raw LLM outputs, provider traces, deterministic validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 hashes so that (a) other researchers can deterministically reproduce the exact run, and (b) follow‑ups that permit independent per‑arm generation and richer validators can be carried out to evaluate the scientific question of GVR repair value under operationally realistic constraints. The artifact bundle supports deterministic forensic analysis of why the shared candidates were accepted and documents the exact experimental boundary that produced the observed outcome.

limitations: Emulation and task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor‑like templates and a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production firmware/device heterogeneity and runtime complexity are not represented.

Single‑model, single‑draw design: only gpt‑5‑mini was used and generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" produced a single LLM candidate per task so repair_attempts = 0; thus the executed confirmatory run did not exercise repair loops.

Validator coverage: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set; untested operational properties (vendor firmware side effects, timing‑dependent behaviors) remain outside the measured construct.

Power‑plan mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure rates; observed baseline success = 100% invalidates the preregistered MDE target and prevents demonstrating the originally planned effect size.

Contamination detection limits: automated token‑overlap checks flagged no confirmatory exclusions, but nondiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be fully excluded.
External generalizability: results under the executed boundary conditions do not generalize to other models, sampling regimes, richer validators, or production heterogeneous device fleets.
